newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National down as dividend disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National down as dividend disappoints.

text.p: Shares in British bank Abbey National Plc fell on Tuesday, weighed down by disappointment over its half-year dividend and signs of margin pressure and market share erosion, analysts said.

The company announced a 23-percent rise in half-year pre-tax profits to 687 million stg, after a charge of 67 million related to changes in the proposed rate of corporation tax. The dividend was raised to 10.2 pence from 8.7.
Analysts had forecast profits between 673 and 700 million and a dividend of between 10.2 and 10.5 pence.
Analysts said the profit figures were reasonably healthy, but the dividend was slightly disappointing. The shares opened 11-1/2p weaker at 798-1/2.

"Although the numbers overall look okay, I think the dividend will be perceived as disappointing," said Panmure Gordon analyst David Poutney. "People were looking for an increase of 20 percent and it's gone up 17. Given that their tier 1 ratio has gone up from 8.5 to 9.2, that's disappointing."

Abbey National's market share of UK mortgages was estimated at 14.3 percent at June 30, up from 12.1 percent at the half-year stage the previous year but down from the full-year 1996 figure of 14.7 percent.
